text: Accounts on a server: sign-up as an option, automatic login with a browser key, upgrade to a permanent login
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: we do implement a user system. Everyone hosts Aimparency and manages users there. "Anyone can create an account" is an option of the server. For Hack the Hub it must be extraordinarily simple: login happens automatically with a key created in the browser's local storage; an exclamation mark recommends upgrading to some permanent type of login.

Today: accounts with name, role and password hash in .bowman/runtime/accounts.json, created by the admin on the command line (accounts.ts); no sign-up, no key login. Earlier thoughts on keys, invitation links and recovery: b9744739.

Assumed by Claude, not said by Felix: accounts belong to the server, not to one graph; the browser key is a key pair, the server stores the public key and the name, and login is a signature; without an upgrade, clearing the browser data loses the account, which is what the exclamation mark warns about.

Not decided: which permanent logins to offer (Felix named password, email and crypto wallet on 2026-11-11), and whether invitation links remain as a third way next to open sign-up and admin-created accounts.

status.comment: Planned 2026-11-12 at Felix's request; nothing built. The kind of permanent login is not decided.
